text:
HSTU already provides a natural temporal mechanism: relative position/time attention bias alongside SiLU-based attention and multiplicative feature gating. Its time bias can learn which elapsed-time ranges matter without imposing uniform decay. The gate is feature interaction, however, not an explicitly supervised estimate that a need has been fulfilled. [Original HSTU paper, 2024](https://arxiv.org/html/2402.17152v3). FuXi-α (WWW 2025) motivates separating temporal, positional and semantic attention channels; this supports richer temporal conditioning but does not establish purchase-completion detection. [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.03036).

T-RoPE (September 2026 preprint) extends HSTU with continuous timestamp rotations, learnable temporal coefficients, multiscale frequencies and calendar-sensitive encoding. Authors report improvements over HSTU with time-relative attention bias, suggesting elapsed time and periodicity provide complementary signals. Its shifted-query training uses next-event timestamps and inference uses current query time, so benchmark adoption requires checking which query-time information is actually available; held-out event timestamps must not be assumed available. [Paper](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.30576v1).

A compatible experiment is a jointly trained, content-conditioned recency gate inside the existing causal HSTU: condition historical contributions on bucketed/log time gaps and the current hidden state, while retaining access to older preferences. Compare positional bias alone, temporal bias, and temporal bias plus gating using the fixed macro validation HR@10. This gate is a proposed hypothesis, not a demonstrated finding from these sources. Interaction histories cannot identify fulfilled needs directly; any benefit would establish predictive temporal adaptation, not verified purchase completion. Keep one network/checkpoint per category and use only timestamps available at prediction.
